vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.30

The MemClaw skill bundle instructs the AI agent to perform high-risk system modifications, including installing an external plugin via the command line (`clawhub:@memclaw/memclaw`) and modifying the global `openclaw.json` configuration to disable native memory features (SKILL.md). While these actions are aligned with the stated purpose of providing a high-performance memory replacement, they utilize the agent as a vector for administrative changes and software installation. The skill also includes tools for reading existing system memory (`cortex_migrate`) and requires local network access to communicate with a background service and a Qdrant database on ports 6333/8085.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions are coherent for a memory plugin, but it asks you to replace the built-in memory and to install an external plugin (source not verified here), which centralizes sensitive data and increases risk — verify the plugin origin and code before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and reference docs consistently describe a drop-in memory backend (cortex:// URIs and cortex_* tools). The declared capabilities match the instructions (search/recall/list/add/commit/migrate). However the registry metadata lists 'Source: unknown' while SKILL.md references a GitHub repo; you should confirm the actual plugin package matches that repo before trusting it.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly tell operators to disable the built-in memory and migrate to MemClaw (set agents.defaults.memorySearch.enabled: false, run cortex_migrate). That is within the declared purpose but represents scope creep from a helper doc to operational change that will cause all agent memories to be stored/managed by the plugin. Because memory can include personal and credential data, this centralization materially raises risk if the plugin is malicious or buggy.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and provides no install spec, but advises running 'openclaw plugins install clawhub:@memclaw/memclaw' which will download and install external code. The skill file does not include or verify that downloaded artifact. Absence of an install manifest means the actual code and its provenance must be checked before installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No env vars, binaries, or config paths are required by the skill itself. The plugin will require LLM/embedding configuration in OpenClaw (user-provided), and the tool APIs operate on cortex://user/... and cortex://session/... URIs (which can contain personal data). The requested access is proportional to a memory backend, but sensitive data exposure depends entirely on the plugin implementation and configured LLM endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation settings are present. Still, the instructions to replace built-in memory and migrate existing memory increase the plugin's long-term access to sensitive data — a higher blast radius if the plugin is malicious or vulnerable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a coherent memory-backend guide, but it asks you to install and make MemClaw the default memory store — which centralizes all agent memory. Before installing or disabling the built-in memory: 1) Verify the plugin package origin (confirm the claimed GitHub repository and that the package you will install matches it). 2) Review the plugin source code (or vendor-supplied binary) for any networking/exfiltration calls and for where data is written. 3) Test the plugin in an isolated environment (non-production agent, with synthetic data). 4) Keep backups of existing OpenClaw memory and do not migrate real secrets until you’ve audited the plugin. 5) Limit or review configured LLM/embedding endpoints and API keys used by the plugin and rotate keys after testing. If you cannot verify the plugin source and code, do not make it the default memory backend.
